SMTO-SYS-0003 — Internal goal mapping failed

GUID: 2e633fac-a485-4a37-9006-f00961f39bc1
Slug: goal-alignment-failed
Domain: SYS · Subsystem: runtime

What happened

  • SMTO had trouble turning your request into steps it could carry out, and stopped. This message does not tell us what caused the problem, or whether any step already ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether your action already happened. Look at the task's activity and at the result itself before doing anything else. Some steps may have run before the problem, and repeating them could do the work twice.
  2. If nothing ran, send the same request again. You don't need to simplify it because of this message. This message comes from SMTO itself, not from how you worded your request.
  3. If you can't tell what happened, or it fails again, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. This message does not establish what completed, so they need the error reference to check before anything is repeated.

What success looks like

  • You've confirmed what the task already did, and the request runs to completion.

If it still fails

  • There is no confirmed quick fix for this message alone. Keep the copied error details for the person investigating, and don't delete the conversation; it holds the record of what happened.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A legacy error text containing 'goal-to-task alignment' was classified into this retained category; no current producer supplies more specific task facts.

What this means

  • Legacy text classification recognizes the phrase goal-to-task alignment and maps it to this retained category; no direct current alignment producer establishes more specific task-acceptance facts. Internal fault classification cannot replace operation effect evidence. A capability may already have dispatched before its adapter faults; neither a runtime defect nor a legacy text label proves that prior work never ran.

Why this can happen

  • Legacy text classification recognizes the phrase goal-to-task alignment and maps it to this retained category; no direct current alignment producer establishes more specific task-acceptance facts.

How to diagnose it

  • Locate the original emitting path and occurrence before attributing the problem to the user's request.

How to fix it

  • No direct repair is available for this occurrence. Use the supported investigation or alternative workflow below.
  • Raised only by _legacy_category in src/agent_runtime/core/user_errors.py for text containing 'goal-to-task alignment', typically from an older SMTO version. Identify the emitting version and the retained task and effect state from the occurrence, report the mapping diagnostic, and do not simplify the request solely because of it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Identify the emitting version and actual retained task/effect state before choosing a continuation.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual mapping defect is diagnosed using retained evidence without unnecessary request simplification.

What not to do

  • Do not delete evidence or invent a configuration change for an unexplained internal failure.

Technical notes

  • Internal fault classification cannot replace operation effect evidence. A capability may already have dispatched before its adapter faults; neither a runtime defect nor a legacy text label proves that prior work never ran.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
